request:
Avoid unconditional process-session isolation for Agent Nodes

## Problem

GitWeave currently launches every Agent Node subprocess with:

```python
start_new_session=True
```

The main reason for creating a separate process session is to support killing the full process group when an explicit execution timeout expires.

However, timeout is now opt-in. Agent Nodes without a configured timeout still receive process-session isolation even though GitWeave has no demonstrated need for it in that case.

This changes normal subprocess behavior preemptively.

## Expected outcome

Do not create a separate process session for Agent Node execution by default.

When no timeout is configured, launch Codex or Claude using normal subprocess behavior.

If an explicit timeout requires process-group termination, enable the minimum process-session/process-group behavior needed for that timeout path.

Conceptually:

```text
No timeout
  → normal Codex / Claude subprocess launch

Explicit timeout
  → enable only the process-group mechanism needed to enforce it
```

Do not add other process-isolation behavior unless a concrete runtime requirement demonstrates that it is necessary.

## Context

The guiding principle is:

> Optional safeguards should not alter the default execution path when the safeguard is not enabled.

This extends the same opt-in timeout principle adopted in #13 and #29.


User directive: GitWeave implements, creates a separate PR, reviews/fixes iteratively and merges only when clean. Stop on unsupported operations or permission/allowance limits and ask the user. No parent manual substitute is authorized.
